title: Mood Instability and Chest Pain
diagnosis: Bipolar disorder — depressive phase with prior manic episode (antidepressant trap risk)
source: U-Word Psychiatry v02 concepts (Immersa rewrite) — anchor for Uber U10
correct_orders: TSH / BMP / tox screen / urine drug screen
ECG + chest pain rule-out (panic vs cardiac)

should_avoid: SSRI or SNRI alone without mood stabilizer
Discharge with passive SI without safety plan

rationale.PHQ-9 / safety assessment (suicide scree: Quantify depression severity and document passive death wishes — mandatory before disposition in young adult with mood crash.
rationale.TSH / BMP / tox screen / urine drug scre: Rule out hyperthyroidism, stimulant use, and metabolic mimics before anchoring on primary mood disorder.
rationale.Mood stabilizer (lithium / valproate): Family history of bipolar and prior manic behavior ( sleepless spending spree ) — mood stabilizer is backbone therapy, not antidepressant alone.
rationale.Avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipo: Classic bipolar trap: antidepressant without stabilizer can precipitate mania or rapid cycling — teach mechanism before prescribing.
rationale.ECG + chest pain rule-out (panic vs card: Last week's ED visit for chest tightness may reflect panic physiology — still obtain ECG and risk-stratify; panic disorder often overlaps mood disorders.
rationale.Lithium level / renal / thyroid monitori: If lithium chosen, plan levels 0.6–1.0 mEq/L, baseline renal function, and TSH — teaching beat for long-term bipolar care.
rationale.Psychiatry referral / disposition by ris: College-age patient with passive SI needs outpatient psychiatry or higher level of care based on risk — document plan and supports.
rationale.SSRI or SNRI alone without mood stabiliz: Dangerous in suspected bipolar — can unmask mania.
rationale.Discharge with passive SI without safety: Passive death wishes require documented safety plan, means restriction, and follow-up within days.

hpi: Jordan Reyes is a 22-year-old college student brought by his roommate for worsening low mood after a dramatic week-long "high." Three weeks ago Jordan stopped sleeping, felt "wired and brilliant," opened two credit cards, and bought a motorcycle he cannot afford — then crashed into exhaustion, guilt, and tearfulness. He now sleeps fourteen hours daily, skips classes, and tells his roommate he "wouldn't mind not waking up" but denies a specific plan. Last week he went to the ED for chest tightness and palpitations; workup was unrevealing and he was told it might be stress. Mother has bipolar disorder treated with lithium. Jordan was started on sertraline by campus health two weeks ago during the low phase — he wonders if it made the earlier "high" worse. No alcohol binge, no illicit drugs, no psychotic symptoms.
hpi_narrative:
Jordan Reyes is a 22-year-old college student brought by his roommate for worsening low mood after a dramatic week-long "high." Three weeks ago Jordan stopped sleeping, felt "wired and brilliant," opened two credit cards, and bought a motorcycle he cannot afford — then crashed into exhaustion, guilt, and tearfulness. He now sleeps fourteen hours daily, skips classes, and tells his roommate he "wouldn't mind not waking up" but denies a specific plan. Last week he went to the ED for chest tightness and palpitations; workup was unrevealing and he was told it might be stress. Mother has bipolar disorder treated with lithium. Jordan was started on sertraline by campus health two weeks ago during the low phase — he wonders if it made the earlier "high" worse. No alcohol binge, no illicit drugs, no psychotic symptoms.

Mechanism: episodic mood elevation with decreased sleep and risky spending fits manic/hypomanic physiology; subsequent crash with neurovegetative symptoms and passive SI fits depressive pole. Antidepressant monotherapy in undiagnosed bipolar can worsen cycling — mood stabilizer first when bipolar is suspected.

Workup: safety screen, TSH/BMP/tox, ECG if chest symptoms recur. Treatment: mood stabilizer (lithium or valproate), psychotherapy, structured follow-up; avoid SSRI alone; address panic-type chest symptoms with CBT/breathing retraining after mood stabilization.
physical_exam: Thin young man, psychomotor slowing, flat affect, poor eye contact when discussing debt
Regular rhythm, no murmur — mild tachycardia when describing chest episode
Non-tender, clear to auscultation — prior chest pain likely non-cardiac at rest today
Alert, oriented, linear thought process, no hallucinations; passive death wishes without plan; denies homicidal ideation

patient_voice.chief_complaint: I can't get out of this hole. My chest freaked me out last week and now I just feel empty.
patient_voice.history: I had this crazy week where I didn't sleep and bought stuff I can't pay for. Now I can barely move. Campus health put me on an antidepressant. My mom has bipolar — I'm scared I'm like her.
patient_voice.pain: My chest was tight last week — like I couldn't breathe — but today it's mostly this heavy sadness.

chief_complaint: Depressive crash after sleepless spending spree, passive death wishes, recent chest tightness
case_summary: College-age man with manic-depressive pattern, family history bipolar, recent SSRI start, passive SI, and prior ED visit for chest pain — mood stabilizer-first workup, safety assessment, panic overlap teaching.
